messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: Fitted values from bym with zeroinflated poisson
parts:
Hi all,

So I've been working with a bym model specified like so:

formula.allcases = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph="nb.sa.txt")

mod.allcases <- inla(formula.allcases, data=as.data.frame(SA), family="poisson", E = exTOT,
                         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1, cdf=c(0)),
                         control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose=TRUE, num.threads = 10,
                     control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd") )

When I run this my mean fitted value is approx 1 as you would expect as the total of obTOT and exTOT are equal:

> summary(mod.allcases$summary.fitted.values[1])
      mean      
 Min.   :0.8498  
 1st Qu.:0.9509  
 Median :0.9881  
 Mean   :1.0003  
 3rd Qu.:1.0441  
 Max.   :1.3667  
>


However because I suspect my obTOT data to be zero inflated, I'm trying the zeroinflated1 family as follows:

mod.allcases <- inla(formula.allcases, data=as.data.frame(SA), family="zeroinflatedpoisson1", E = exTOT,
                         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1, cdf=c(0)),
                         control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose=TRUE, num.threads = 10,
                     control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd") )

It runs fine but my mean fitted values are larger than one which I'm confused about:

> summary(mod.allcases$summary.fitted.values[1])
      mean      
 Min.   :1.269  
 1st Qu.:1.293  
 Median :1.309  
 Mean   :1.309  
 3rd Qu.:1.323  
 Max.   :1.395  
>


Why are the fitted values not centered on 1 for the zero inflated poisson model?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitted values from bym with zeroinflated poisson
parts:
On Sun, 2019-01-20 at 05:27 -0800, jpkrooney wrote:
>
> Why are the fitted values not centered on 1 for the zero inflated
> poisson model?
>

because the linear predictor only relates to the non-zero part, and do not add the
prob of observing zero. I think the fitted values are still E*exp(eta) without correcting
for the prob of being zero.

--

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitted values from bym with zeroinflated poisson
parts:
Yes, you need to compute the relative risk yourself, unless you're
happy with the E*exp(\eta) one, which is just a scaled version of the
Expected value when you include the zero-inflation.

You can extract the zero-probability from the fit, yes.

Strictly, there is a dependence of the zero-prob and the linear
predictor, and if you want/need to account for that, you have to rely
on using inla.posterior.sample, like this small example



data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
form = Y ~ f(region,model="besag",graph=g)
r = inla(form, family="zeroinflatedpoisson1", data=Germany, E=E,
control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

ysim.fun = function(...)
{
args = list(...)
prob = theta[1]
n = length(Predictor)
return (prob + (1-prob) * rpois(n, lambda = args$E *
exp(Predictor)))
}
xx = inla.posterior.sample(10000, r)
yy = inla.posterior.sample.eval(ysim.fun, xx, E=Germany$E)
y.mean = apply(yy,1,mean)
germany.map(y.mean/Germany$E)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitted values from bym with zeroinflated poisson
parts:
Note that that code won't give you samples from the posterior; only
samples for which the posterior expectation (I believe) is correct,
but the variance etc will not be.
For full posterior samples one needs to sample a 0/1 variable for the
zero inflation:

rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 1-prob) * rpois(n, lambda = ...)

Since the zero-probability is constant, I wouldn't expect that to
change the spatial pattern; only the general variability.

(I'm involved with a project where zero-inflated poisson likelihood
interacts with multiple random effects, where we are looking at a
variance reduced, Rao-Blackwellised version, for the posterior mean
and variance, but it's not publicly available yet.)

Finn

parts: That's great thank you Havard!
On Monday, January 21, 2019 at 4:23:14 PM UTC, INLA help wrote:

For completeness I post here a correct code that does not only allow to
estimate the mean. I know the function can be written more compact, but
I like to write things a little out so I understand it later...

H


On Mon, 2019-01-21 at 06:43 -0800, jpkrooney wrote:
> OK great thanks! 👍
>
> On Monday, January 21, 2019 at 2:41:47 PM UTC, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> > Hi,
> > That looks like a most likely harmless commentary from the Matrix
> > package. INLA converts to a specific sparse matrix format when it
> > needs to.
> >
> > Finn
> >
> > On 21 Jan 2019, at 14:32, jpkrooney <jpkr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > > Guys one last question.
> > >
> > > WhenI try to run a bym2 with zeroinflated1 I get the following
> > > ominous warning
> > >
> > > formula.allcases = obTOT ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym2",
> > > graph="nb.sa.txt")
> > >
> > > > mod.allcases <- inla(formula.allcases, data=as.data.frame(SA),
> > > family="zeroinflatedpoisson1", E = exTOT,
> > > +                          control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,
> > > link=1, cdf=c(0)),
> > > +                          control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,
> > > cpo=TRUE, config = TRUE), verbose=TRUE, num.threads = 10,
> > > +                      control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd")
> > > )
> > > x[.,.] <- val : x being coerced from Tsparse* to CsparseMatrix
> > >
> > >
> > > It still runs to completion, but I wasn't sure how worried I
> > > should be about this ?
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Monday, January 21, 2019 at 1:55:43 PM UTC, Helpdesk wrote:
> > > > correct. thank you.
> > > >
> > > > On Mon, 2019-01-21 at 13:07 +0000, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> > > > > Note that that code won't give you samples from the
> > > > posterior; only
> > > > > samples for which the posterior expectation (I believe) is
> > > > correct,
> > > > > but the variance etc will not be.
> > > > > For full posterior samples one needs to sample a 0/1 variable
> > > > for the
> > > > > zero inflation:
> > > > >
> > > > > rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 1-prob) * rpois(n, lambda = ...)
> > > > >
> > > > > Since the zero-probability is constant, I wouldn't expect
> > > > that to
> > > > > change the spatial pattern; only the general variability.
> > > > >
> > > > > (I'm involved with a project where zero-inflated poisson
> > > > likelihood
> > > > > interacts with multiple random effects, where we are looking
> > > > at a
> > > > > variance reduced, Rao-Blackwellised version, for the
> > > > posterior mean
> > > > > and variance, but it's not publicly available yet.)
> > > > >
> > > > > Finn
> > > > >
> > > > > On Mon, 21 Jan 2019 at 12:53, jpkrooney <jpkr...@gmail.com>
> > > > wrote:
> > > > > > Ok so that gives me a much more uniform result:
> > > > > > > summary(SA$RRall)
> > > > > >    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.
> > > > > >  0.0000  0.9824  1.0029  1.0035  1.0237  3.3387
> > > > > >
> > > > > > This is not really what I expected since now there is no
> > > > pattern.
> > > > > > But I guess it means the zeroinflated model explains the
> > > > data well?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > About the code: prob *0 - isn't that just always =0?
> > > > > > So doesn't the equation simplified to:
> > > > > >  (1-prob) * rpois(...))
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Monday, January 21, 2019 at 11:51:23 AM UTC, Helpdesk
> > > > wrote:
> > > > > > > On Mon, 2019-01-21 at 03:30 -0800, jpkrooney wrote:
> > > > > > > >     return (prob + (1-prob) * rpois(n, lambda = args$E
> > > > *
> > > > > > > >                                        
> > > > exp(Predictor)))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > it should of-course be
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >         (prob * 0 + (1-prob) * rpois(...))
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
